newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Western primary nickel ouptut up in December -INSG.
newsitem.headline: Western primary nickel ouptut up in December -INSG.

text.p: Western world primary nickel output edged up to 61,400 tonnes in December from 59,500 a month earlier, reflecting increases in South Africa, Norway, Colombia and Australia, the International Nickel Study Group (INSG) said.

South African output rose 300 tonnes to 3,000 and Norway's was up 600 to 5,600 tonnes. Colombian production was 700 tonnes higher at 2,600 and Australia's increased to 7,100 from 6,700 tonnes, it said in its latest monthly bulletin.
These rises outweighed small output declines in Canada -- where output dipped to 12,000 tonnes from 12,400 and in Japan -- where production slipped 200 tonnes to 11,200.
The figures take the 1996 western world year total to 681,000 tonnes, up sharply on 1995's 654,000 tonnes.
On the consumption side, western world offtake also rose against the November total, rising to 73,500 tonnes from 72,100.

U.S. and European Union consumption was static at 13,000 tonnes and 25,700 tonnes respectively but Japanese offtake rose 400 tonnes to a strong 17,200, equalling its highest monthly total of the year.
INSG said western world consumption for the whole of 1996 was pegged at 852,500 tonnes down from 900,000 tonnes in 1995. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
